title: The focus system as a system
objectives: See actor, object, locative and benefactive focus laid out side by side as one system
Say the same event in all four focuses and feel the difference in meaning
Choose the focus based on what is definite, known or emphasized
Handle the aspect forms of -in, -an and i- verbs confidently, including irregular-looking ones

grammar.title: One event, four spotlights: the map of the system
grammar.explanation:
Everything you learned about mag-, -um-, -in and -an verbs in A2 was one system all along. A Tagalog sentence has exactly one ang-phrase, and the verb's affix tells you which role that ang-phrase plays. Think of the affix as a spotlight: the event is the same, but the spotlight lands on a different participant.

Actor focus (mag-, -um-, ma-): the spotlight is on the doer. Object focus (-in): the spotlight is on the thing acted on. Locative focus (-an): the spotlight is on a place, source, or the person on the receiving end. Benefactive/theme focus (i-): the spotlight is on the thing handed over or the person you do something for.

English does something similar with the passive ('The dog bit the man' vs 'The man was bitten by the dog') but Tagalog has four regular options instead of two, and uses them constantly. Choosing the focus is not optional decoration — it is how Tagalog signals what the sentence is about. The other participants do not disappear; they just get demoted to ng-phrases (doer or indefinite object) or sa-phrases (location, recipient).

examples.tl: Bumili ang bata ng tinapay.
examples.en: The child bought (some) bread. (spotlight: the child)

examples.tl: Binili ng bata ang tinapay.
examples.en: The child bought the bread. (spotlight: the bread)

examples.tl: Binilhan ng bata ang panaderya.
examples.en: The child bought (something) from the bakery. (spotlight: the bakery)

examples.tl: Ibinili ng bata ng tinapay ang lola.
examples.en: The child bought bread for grandma. (spotlight: grandma)

grammar.title: The same event in all four focuses
grammar.explanation:
Take one real-life event: Ana bought fish at the market for her mother. Every participant can take a turn under the spotlight.

Actor focus answers 'Who bought?': Bumili si Ana ng isda sa palengke para sa nanay niya. Here 'ng isda' is indefinite — some fish, fish in general.

Object focus answers 'What did Ana buy?': Binili ni Ana ang isda sa palengke. Now the fish is 'the fish' — a specific one both speakers know about. Ana demotes to ni Ana.

Locative focus answers 'Where did Ana buy / whom did she buy from?': Binilhan ni Ana ng isda ang palengke, or more naturally with a person, Binilhan ni Ana ng isda si Mang Tomas — she bought fish from Mang Tomas. With -an, the sa-phrase gets promoted to ang.

Benefactive focus answers 'Who did Ana buy it for?': Ibinili ni Ana ng isda ang nanay niya — she bought fish for her mother.

Notice what stays constant: the doer is ang in actor focus and ng everywhere else; the thing bought is ang in object focus and ng everywhere else. Only the spotlight moves. If you can transform one sentence through all four focuses, you own the core of Tagalog grammar.

examples.tl: Bumili si Ana ng isda sa palengke para sa nanay niya.
examples.en: Ana bought fish at the market for her mother.

examples.tl: Binili ni Ana ang isda sa palengke.
examples.en: Ana bought the fish at the market.

examples.tl: Binilhan ni Ana ng isda si Mang Tomas.
examples.en: Ana bought fish from Mang Tomas.

examples.tl: Ibinili ni Ana ng isda ang nanay niya.
examples.en: Ana bought fish for her mother.

examples.tl: Sino ang bumili ng isda?
examples.en: Who bought fish? (actor question, actor-focus answer)

examples.tl: Ano ang binili ni Ana?
examples.en: What did Ana buy? (object question, object-focus answer)

grammar.title: Choosing the focus: definiteness and emphasis
grammar.explanation:
The single most useful rule: the ang-phrase is definite — 'the', not 'a'. So when the object is specific and known, Tagalog strongly prefers object focus. 'I ate the adobo (that you cooked)' is Kinain ko ang adobo, not Kumain ako ng adobo, which means 'I ate (some) adobo'. In fact, a ng-object can never be definite, so 'Kumain ako ng adobo mo' for 'I ate your adobo' sounds off — a possessed object is definite, so you need Kinain ko ang adobo mo.

Second rule: questions and answers match focus. Ano ang...? and Sino ang...? put the questioned thing in the ang slot, so the verb must focus it: Ano ang niluto mo? — Niluto ko ang sinigang. Answering with the wrong focus sounds like answering a different question.

Third rule: commands follow the same logic. Bumili ka ng gatas — buy (some) milk, any milk. Bilhin mo ang gatas — buy the milk (the one we talked about). Hugasan mo ang mga pinggan — the dishes are definite, so -an focus.

When both readings are possible, Tagalog leans heavily toward the non-actor focuses in everyday speech; overusing actor focus is the classic learner accent. When in doubt and the object is 'the', go object focus.

examples.tl: Kumain ako ng mangga.
examples.en: I ate a mango / some mango.

examples.tl: Kinain ko ang mangga.
examples.en: I ate the mango.

examples.tl: Ano ang binili mo? — Binili ko ang sapatos na ito.
examples.en: What did you buy? — I bought these shoes.

examples.tl: Bilhin mo ang gatas sa pinakamalapit na tindahan.
examples.en: Buy the milk at the nearest store.

examples.tl: Hugasan mo muna ang mga pinggan.
examples.en: Wash the dishes first.

examples.tl: Isara mo ang pinto, malamig na.
examples.en: Close the door, it's cold already.

grammar.title: Aspect across the focuses, plus ma- actor verbs
grammar.explanation:
You already know the aspect patterns from A2; here is the whole table in one place so you can generate any form.

-in verbs: completed puts -in- after the first consonant (binili), incompleted adds syllable doubling (binibili), contemplated doubles and keeps the -in suffix (bibilhin). Note the suffix often shortens the root: bili + hin = bilhin, dala + hin = dalhin. Roots starting with l or w often use ni- instead of the infix: niluto, niluluto, lulutuin.

-an verbs work the same but keep -an in every form: hinugasan, hinuhugasan, huhugasan; binilhan, binibilhan, bibilhan.

i- verbs keep i- up front: ibinigay, ibinibigay, ibibigay; isinara, isinasara, isasara.

Finally, meet ma- actor-focus verbs — a small but very common family: matulog (sleep), maligo (bathe), maupo (sit), matakot (be afraid). They conjugate na-/na+doubling/ma+doubling: natulog, natutulog, matutulog. Don't confuse this actor ma- with other ma- meanings you'll meet in the next unit; for now, just learn these as everyday actor verbs.

examples.tl: Niluto niya ang hapunan kagabi.
examples.en: She cooked the dinner last night.

examples.tl: Lulutuin ko ang adobo bukas.
examples.en: I will cook the adobo tomorrow.

examples.en: We buy vegetables from Aling Nena every Saturday.

examples.tl: Ibinibigay niya ang lumang damit sa mga kapitbahay.
examples.en: She gives the old clothes to the neighbors.

examples.tl: Natutulog pa ang sanggol.

examples.tl: Maliligo muna ako bago tayo umalis.
examples.en: I'll take a bath first before we leave.

example.tl: Bumili kami ng prutas sa palengke.
example.en: We bought fruit at the market.

example.tl: Hiniwa niya nang manipis ang sibuyas.

dialogue.title: Sa palengke
dialogue.context: Ana takes her friend Ben, a foreigner learning Tagalog, on his first trip to the wet market.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Dito tayo bibili ng isda. Suki ko ang may-ari ng puwestong iyan.
lines.en: We'll buy fish here. The owner of that stall is my suki.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Ano ang bibilhin natin, ang tilapia o ang bangus?
lines.en: What are we buying, the tilapia or the milkfish?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Bilhin natin ang bangus. Mas sariwa iyan ngayong umaga.
lines.en: Let's buy the milkfish. It's fresher this morning.

lines.speaker: Mang Tomas
lines.tl: Ana! Bumili ka ulit ng bangus? Magaganda ang dating ngayon.
lines.en: Ana! Buying milkfish again? Today's arrivals are beautiful.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Opo, Mang Tomas. Ibibili ko rin po ng hipon ang nanay ko.
lines.en: Yes, Mang Tomas. I'll also buy shrimp for my mom.

lines.speaker: Mang Tomas
lines.tl: Sige, itimbang ko na. Heto ang sukli mo.
lines.en: Sure, let me weigh it. Here's your change.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Ana, bakit 'binilhan' ang sabi mo kanina, hindi 'binili'?
lines.en: Ana, why did you say 'binilhan' earlier, not 'binili'?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Magkaiba ang kahulugan. Binili ko ang isda, pero binilhan ko si Mang Tomas.
lines.en: They mean different things. I bought the fish, but I bought from Mang Tomas.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Ah, iba ang naka-focus sa bawat pangungusap!
lines.en: Ah, a different thing is in focus in each sentence!

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Tama. Tapos kapag para sa ibang tao, 'ibinili'. Ibinili kita ng turon, o.
lines.en: Right. And when it's for someone else, 'ibinili'. Look, I bought you a turon.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.tl: Salamat! Sige, uuwi na tayo? Luluto na ba natin ang bangus?
lines.en: Thanks! Okay, shall we head home? Are we cooking the milkfish now?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.tl: Oo. Ikaw ang maghuhugas ng mga sangkap, ako ang magluluto.
lines.en: Yes. You'll wash the ingredients, I'll do the cooking.

reading.title: Ang Sabado ni Aling Rosa
reading.tl:
Tuwing Sabado, pumupunta si Aling Rosa sa palengke. Bumibili siya ng gulay, isda, at karne para sa buong linggo. Kaninang umaga, binili niya ang pinakasariwang bangus sa puwesto ni Mang Tomas. Suki niya ito, kaya laging tama ang sukli at may kaunting dagdag pa. Binilhan din niya ng prutas ang bagong tindahan sa kanto dahil mura raw doon ang presyo. Bago umuwi, ibinili niya ng tsokolate ang kaniyang apo dahil kaarawan nito bukas.

Pag-uwi, nagluto si Aling Rosa ng sinigang. Hinugasan muna niya ang mga gulay, saka hiniwa ang karne. Habang niluluto niya ang ulam, inayos naman ng kaniyang anak ang mesa at hinugasan ang mga pinggan. Masaya ang hapunan nila dahil kumpleto ang pamilya.
reading.en:
Every Saturday, Aling Rosa goes to the market. She buys vegetables, fish, and meat for the whole week. This morning, she bought the freshest milkfish at Mang Tomas's stall. She is his regular customer, so the change is always right and there's even a little extra. She also bought fruit from the new store on the corner because they say the prices there are cheap. Before going home, she bought chocolate for her grandchild because it's the child's birthday tomorrow.

When she got home, Aling Rosa cooked sinigang. First she washed the vegetables, then sliced the meat. While she was cooking the dish, her child set the table and washed the plates. Their dinner was a happy one because the family was complete.

exercises.prompt: In 'Binili ng bata ang tinapay', which participant is under the spotlight (in focus)?
exercises.explain: The -in verb binili puts the object in the ang slot: ang tinapay is the focused, definite element.

exercises.prompt: You want to say 'I ate the adobo' (a specific adobo you both know about). Which is correct?
exercises.explain: A definite object ('the adobo') goes in the ang slot, which requires the object-focus verb kinain. Kumain ako ng adobo means 'I ate some adobo'.

exercises.prompt: Sino ang ___ ng isda? (Who bought fish? — use the actor-focus completed form of bili)
exercises.hint: Sino ang...? asks about the actor, so the verb must be actor focus.
exercises.explain: Sino ang...? puts the actor in the ang slot, so the verb must be actor focus: bumili.

exercises.prompt: Ano ang ___ mo sa palengke? (What did you buy at the market?)
exercises.hint: Ano ang...? asks about the object.
exercises.explain: Ano ang...? puts the object in the ang slot, so the verb must be object focus: binili.

exercises.prompt: 'Binilhan ni Ana ng isda si Mang Tomas.' What does this sentence say?
choices: Ana bought fish for Mang Tomas.
Ana bought fish from Mang Tomas.
Mang Tomas bought fish from Ana.
exercises.explain: The -an verb binilhan focuses the source: si Mang Tomas is the person Ana bought from. 'For Mang Tomas' would be ibinili.

exercises.tl: Ibinili ko ng bagong sapatos ang kapatid ko.
choices: Bought new shoes for their sibling
Bought new shoes from their sibling
exercises.explain: Ibinili is the benefactive focus of bili: the focused ang-phrase (ang kapatid ko) is the person the shoes were bought for.

exercises.prompt: ___ mo ang mga pinggan pagkatapos kumain. (Wash the dishes after eating — command form)
exercises.hint: The dishes are definite, so use the -an verb's base form.
exercises.explain: Commands with a definite object use the non-actor focus infinitive: Hugasan mo ang mga pinggan.

exercises.prompt: I will cook the adobo tomorrow.
exercises.explain: 'The adobo' is definite, so object focus; contemplated aspect of lutuin is lulutuin (doubling + -in suffix).

exercises.prompt: Which sentence sounds wrong to a native speaker?
choices: Kakainin ko ang mansanas na ito.
exercises.explain: A possessed object (mansanas mo, 'your apple') is definite, and a ng-object cannot be definite — so it must be Kinain ko ang mansanas mo.

exercises.prompt: Binilhan ko ng pandesal ang panaderya sa kanto.
exercises.answer: I bought pandesal from the bakery on the corner.
accept: I bought pandesal from the bakery on the corner
I bought bread from the bakery on the corner
I bought pandesal at the bakery on the corner
I bought some pandesal from the corner bakery
exercises.explain: Binilhan (locative focus) promotes the source — the bakery — to the ang slot; the pandesal stays indefinite as a ng-phrase.

exercises.tl: Isinara na ng guwardiya ang gate kaya doon tayo sa likod dumaan.
choices: The guard opened the gate for us
The guard already closed the gate, so we'll go through the back
The guard is closing the back gate
We asked the guard to open the gate
exercises.explain: Isinara (i- verb, completed) plus na means the gate is already closed; kaya introduces the consequence — going around the back.

exercises.prompt: Ana bought fish for her mother. (use the benefactive focus)
exercises.answer: Ibinili ni Ana ng isda ang nanay niya.
accept: Ibinili ni Ana ng isda ang nanay niya
Ibinili ni Ana ang nanay niya ng isda
Ibinili ng isda ni Ana ang nanay niya
Ibinili ni Ana ng isda ang kanyang nanay
Ibinili ni Ana ng isda ang kaniyang nanay
exercises.explain: The beneficiary (her mother) takes the ang slot with i- focus: ibinili. Ana demotes to ni Ana and the fish to ng isda.
